The '''1899 Puerto Rico census''' ('''Porto Rico''' was also used) was a [[United States Census|national population census held in Puerto Rico]] and first under [[United States|U.S.]] control by the [[U.S. Census Bureau]] for the U.S. War Department.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/history/www/faqs/demographic_faqs/when_was_puerto_rico_first_included_in_the_us_census.html|title=When was Puerto Rico first included in a census of the United States?|date=1900|work=United States Census Bureau|access-date=December 27, 2019}}</ref> It was the tenth census combined with the nine previous censuses taken by [[Spain]]. 
The day used for the census was Friday November 10, 1899 with a total population counted as 953,243 - an increase of 154,678 or 16% over the previous [[1887 Puerto Rico census|1887 census]] taken by the [[Spanish government]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/40/mode/2up|title=Report on the census of Porto Rico 1899|page=40|date=1900|access-date=December 27, 2019}}</ref>

==Population schedule==
[[File:Enumerators of Arecibo.jpg|230px|thumb|Enumerators of [[Arecibo]].]]
The population schedule used in the census, translated into English and reduced in size is as follows:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/37/mode/1up |title=Report on the census of Porto Rico Population schedule|page=37|accessdate= November 26, 2023}}</ref><br>
'''Situation'''
*Street.
*Number of house.
*Number of house or building in the order of visitation.
*Number of family in the order of visitation.
*Name of every person residing with this family or in this house
'''Relationship'''
*Relationship of each person to the head of the family.
'''Personal description'''
*[[Color terminology for race|Color]]. 
*[[Gender identity|Sex]].
*[[Population ageing|Age]] at last birthday.
*Status.
'''Nativity'''
*Native country of this person.
'''Citizenship'''
*[[Cubans|Cuban]], [[Spaniards|Spaniard]], or in suspense.
'''Occupation'''
*Occupation, trade or profession of every person 10 years of age and over.
'''Instruction'''
*Months of attendance at school during the last school year.
*Can read. (primary)
*Can write. (primary)
*Higher.
'''Sanitary conditions'''
*Source of water used.
*Disposition of garbage.
*[[Latrine]] system.

==Method of tabulation==
It was taken that to save time, the tabulation should be done by machine and not by the old hand-tally system. As the machines invented by Mr [[Herman Hollerith]] were successfully used in the earlier eleventh and were to be used for the twelfth U.S. census, it was adopted.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/37/mode/1up|title=1899 census of Puerto Rico: Method of Tabulation|page=38|accessdate=15 June 2024}}</ref>

The number of foreign-born returned by the census is 13,872 or about 1.5% of the total population. There were few regions in the [[Western Hemisphere]] in which the proportion of natives is so high and that of the foreign-born so low. Of the total number of foreigners 5,935 or 43 per cent were found in the three cities of [[San Juan, Puerto Rico|San Juan]], [[Ponce, Puerto Rico|Ponce]] and [[Mayagüez, Puerto Rico|Mayagüez]]. 
Of the total foreign-born, 7,690 or 55% were born in Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/62/mode/2up |title=Report on the census of Porto Rico 1899|page=63|accessdate= November 26, 2023}}</ref>

===Race===
With reference to [[Race (human categorization)|race]], the population of Porto Rico is divided by the census into two main classes - those who are and those who are not  [[White Puerto Ricans|White]].
The number belonging to each of these classes is as follows:<ref name="archive.org">{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/58/mode/2up |title=Report on the census of Porto Rico, 1899 Census of "Porto Rico"|page=57|accessdate= November 26, 2023}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:right"
|-
! Race
! Population
! %
|-
|align=left| [[White Puerto Ricans|White]] || 589,426|| 61.8
|- align=right
|align=left| Colored*  || 363,817 || 38.2
|-
|align=left| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; ''(Persons of [[Multiracial|mixed]] blood)'' || ''304,352''|| ''83.6''
|-
!align=left| Puerto Rico||align=center| 953,243 ||align=center| 100.0
|}
The colored in the table includes very few (75) [[Chinese immigration to Puerto Rico|Chinese]] and many persons of mixed white and Black African blood as well as pure Black. Somewhat more than three-fifths of the population of Porto Rico are white and nearly two-fifths are partly or  entirely African or Black. By the 1899 census five-sixths (83.6 per cent) of the total colored were returned as of mixed blood.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/56/mode/2up |title=Report on the census of Porto Rico 1899|page=56|accessdate= November 26, 2023}}</ref>
